relations.subject: capella-role:organization-owner
relations.evidence: Organization Owners automatically have the [Project Owner](../projects/project-roles.md#project-owner-role) project role for all projects in the organization.

relations.subject: capella-role:project-creator
relations.evidence: Has all privileges granted by the [Organization Member](#organization-role-member) role

relations.subject: capella-role:project-creator
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (impliesRole) - conditional on projects the Project Creator itself creates, narrower than Organization Owner's blanket implication over all projects
relations.evidence: Project Creators automatically have the [Project Owner](../projects/project-roles.md#project-owner-role) project role for any project that they create.

relations.subject: capella:organization
relations.evidence: An organization must have at least one user with the **Organization Owner** role at all times.

notable_absence.finding: The organization-role catalog itself carries no support-plan or edition gating - all three roles (Organization Owner, Project Creator, Organization Member) are available regardless of plan or edition; gating by plan/role is described elsewhere (e.g. SSO requiring a paid Support Plan) but not here. No edition badges or server-version-string citations either (both known recurring anomalies absent).

cross_component_finding: Directly answers this batch's key hypothesis: organization-user-roles.md's own table names THREE organization roles - Organization Owner, Project Creator, Organization Member - and only ONE of these (Organization Owner) matches a name in the prior capella-role:* catalog built from SQL++ statement Prerequisites sections (organization-owner/project-owner/project-data-writer). Project Owner and Project Data Writer, it turns out, were never organization roles at all in this page's own taxonomy - they are PROJECT roles (defined on the separate, linked-but-not-read project-roles.md) that Organization Owner and Project Creator each automatically imply (see impliesRole relations above). So the 'disjunctive gate over three capella-role:* values' seen on statement pages is actually a gate over a mix of two organization roles' implied project role (organization-owner, project-creator-when-implying) plus one native project role (project-owner) plus one more native project role (project-data-writer) - the statement-page gate silently flattens two distinct catalogs (organization roles and project roles) into one list. This is a genuine, previously invisible modeling gap: the capella-role:* namespace as currently promoted conflates an organization-role catalog and a project-role catalog that the Organizations UI docs keep strictly separate. Recommend the reconciler split capella-role:* into capella-org-role:* (organization-owner, project-creator, organization-member) and capella-project-role:* (project-owner, project-data-writer, cluster-manager, and whatever else project-roles.md defines) rather than treating all five+ as one flat scheme.
